security_audit.summary: All 51 static findings are false positives covering Markdown, documented service calls, normal credential storage, and model descriptions. A separate semantic finding identifies unsafe prompt interpolation in shell examples, compounded by an unsupported assurance that prompt content cannot cause shell injection. The external CLI implementation was unavailable, so its claimed protections were not independently verified.

remediation.issue: Shell examples embed arbitrary prompts inside single-quoted JSON arguments without shell-safe handling.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize input with a JSON library and invoke the CLI with an argument array, without a shell; test apostrophes and shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The input-boundary section claims no shell injection surface without addressing the calling shell.
remediation.suggestion: Distinguish CLI parsing from shell parsing and replace the blanket assurance with explicit safe invocation guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Interpolation Guidance for User Prompts
semantic_findings.description: Examples embed '<user prompt>' inside single-quoted JSON shell arguments without escaping guidance. Verbatim substitution permits apostrophes to terminate shell quoting and introduce commands. The claim 'No shell injection surface from prompt content' overlooks parsing by the calling shell.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples visibly place prompt placeholders inside shell single quotes, and the safety claim ignores caller-side parsing. Exploitation depends on verbatim substitution; no executable wrapper was supplied.

content.value_statement: Image drafts need clear prompts and consistent generation settings. This skill guides Nano Banana 2 requests through RunComfy for batches, typography, framing, and refinement.
actual_capabilities: Guide text-to-image requests through the RunComfy CLI using the documented Nano Banana 2 endpoint.
Configure batches of one to four images, including low-resolution ideation rounds.
Select documented aspect ratios, four resolution tiers, and PNG, JPEG, or WebP output.
Structure subject-first prompts with explicit text placement and typography instructions.
Reuse seed values during prompt refinement and enable optional web grounding.
Explain authentication options, output directories, model selection, and documented CLI exit codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, authentication, internet access, and paid service usage; no CLI implementation is bundled.
Produces still images only; preserving an existing subject through editing requires a separate endpoint.
Supports at most four images per request and only the documented resolution tiers and aspect ratios.
Higher resolutions and web grounding increase cost; image quality, text accuracy, and exact reproducibility are not guaranteed.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Create a Square Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate one square 1K PNG with Nano Banana 2: a red ceramic mug on a white table, soft daylight, clean studio photography.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first image request with explicit output settings.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Render a Headline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 16:9 product-card draft with a black ceramic mug. Place the exact headline "Brewed Quietly" at the top right in bold sans-serif.
prompt_templates.scenario: A graphic requiring exact text and deliberate placement.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Compare a Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate four 9:16 concepts at 0.5K for a tea campaign: one ceramic cup, morning side-light, minimal composition. Keep web search disabled.
prompt_templates.scenario: Low-resolution batch exploration before selecting a direction.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Refine with Controlled Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine this prompt: [approved prompt]. Generate one 2K 16:9 WebP with seed 42. Disable web search. Confirm cost before submitting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A controlled final request after prompt approval.

output_examples.input: Create four vertical tea campaign drafts at 0.5K.
output: Expected deliverable: four generated still images in the selected output directory.
Request settings: 9:16 framing, 0.5K resolution, and web grounding disabled.

output_examples.input: Generate a wide product card with the headline "Brewed Quietly" at 2K.
output: Expected deliverable: one 16:9 product-card image with the requested headline and product composition.
Review the generated lettering and layout before using the image publicly.

best_practices: Start with the subject, then specify setting, style, framing, and exact text placement.
Use low-resolution drafts first; confirm image count, resolution, web-search settings, and expected cost before submission.
Keep credentials private, avoid confidential prompts, and serialize JSON into shell-free CLI arguments rather than interpolating prompt text.
anti_patterns: Paste arbitrary user prompts directly into single-quoted shell command examples.
Use this text-to-image endpoint to preserve an existing subject identity or edit an uploaded image.
Request unsupported dimensions or enable web grounding and high resolutions without checking cost.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It guides still-image generation with Google Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy CLI, including drafts, product graphics, and text-bearing images.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual generation also requires a working RunComfy CLI and authenticated account.

faq.question: Does it edit existing images or create videos?
faq.answer: No. This endpoint generates still images from text. Image editing requires the separate edit endpoint or sibling skill.

faq.question: How many images can I request?
faq.answer: The documented limit is four images per request. Available resolution tiers are 0.5K, 1K, 2K, and 4K.

faq.question: Does generation run locally?
faq.answer: No. The local CLI sends prompts to the hosted RunComfy Model API and downloads generated results. Avoid submitting confidential information.

faq.question: Is web search required, and does it affect cost?
faq.answer: Web grounding is optional and disabled by default. Enabling it adds cost and latency; higher resolution tiers also cost more.
